title: Kernel morning bullet triage — Vivian Park
content:
Quick morning dump — goal: triage open regressions, set 2-hour experiments, and clear obvious low-effort TODOs.

Context: small traffic spike yesterday triggered increased tail latency in the 512->1k token path. On-call flagged higher kernel mutex contention in queue manager. I took a quick look at flame graphs (attached in PR) and sketched immediate hypotheses below.

What I saw (quick):
- 22:14UTC spike correlated with cache miss storms on /v1/generate for model-owl-13b-quant.
- KV cache eviction rate jumped ~3x for warm prefixes (see Linear RINF-762).
- Flame: ~55% time in kv_cache::evict() and btree lock acquisitions in batch_router.
- s390 (internal test cluster) reproduced with small repro script (link above).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Eviction thrash: small batch requests with interleaved long-context requests evict prefixes before subsequent requests can reuse them. -> increases backend work and lock churn.
2) Lock granularity: single global rack-level lock in btree causes blocking under high concurrency. Might be able to sharded-lock by shard-id.
3) Cold quant path fallback: some requests hit a slower kernel path due to quantization selection mismatch (model variant fingerprinting bug).

Immediate actions (today — 2hr sprint blocks):
- [ ] Re-run repro with instrumentation at evict() boundaries and add per-prefix hit counter (2h) — ASSIGNED: Vivian
  - cmd: ./tools/repro_kv_storm --model owl-13b-quant --qps 80 --concurrency 48 --seed 42
  - metrics to capture: evictions/sec, hit_ratio_by_prefix, lock_wait_ms
- [ ] Quick patch to reduce eviction window: increase prefix retention TTL from 5s -> 12s in runtime config (can be toggled with feature flag) (1h) — ASSIGNED: Kyla
- [ ] Add metric for avg lock hold time on batch_router_lock (instrumentation PR #1987) (1.5h) — ASSIGNED: Diego

Notes on experiments:
- If TTL bump reduces evictions by >40% and tail latency improves, we promote as short-term mitigation. Risk: memory pressure on dense multi-tenant hosts. Need mem cap guard.
- If lock hold times are high (>2ms per op under contention) -> consider split by prefix hash. This is medium effort (3–4d).

Low-effort cleanup (do now):
- [ ] Add a short comment in batch_router explaining why current global lock exists (prevent accidental reverts) — (15m)
- [ ] Close stale Linear cards linked to previous eviction experiment (RINF-621) — (10m)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Which customer tenants were on the affected host? Need to correlate with billing tags. Action: ask SRE to map host -> tenant (Diego).
- Is this specific to owl-13b-quant or wide across quantized models? We have partial logs for llama-2-13b-quant but not for mosaic-quant. Add a sampling hook.

Temporary mitigations to consider (if spike recurs):
- Route short requests to a low-latency cache-tier (hot shards) instead of general pool. Needs routing policy change (product).
- Throttle concurrent writes to KV cache per-prefix (soft backpressure) — cheap but could increase client-side timeouts.

Quick mental checklist before pairing with Kyla:
- verify feature-flag rollout path (console + infra toggle)
- ensure TTL experiment has a rollback TTL default of 5s and alert when mem per-host > 85%
- capture perf baseline window (last 24h) to compare — take snapshot now

Scratch commands & snippets I ran: (saved in terminal)
- ssh s390-01 'sudo perf record -F 99 -p $(pgrep runtime) -g -- sleep 30'
- ./tools/evict_instrument --dump --out /tmp/evict.dump
- jq '.events | map(select(.type=="evict")) | length' /tmp/evict.dump

Follow-ups (by end of day):
- Kyla: rolling TTL flag to canary hosts (2 nodes) + mem guard (PR + smoke tests)
- Diego: lock hold metric + dashboard tile + compare pre/post
- Vivian (me): write short postmortem stub if TTL bump helps. Draft link: confluence://rinf/pm-notes/kv-eviction-prelim

Misc notes / brain dump:
- Consider gradual degrade: when eviction rate spikes, fall back to smaller batch sizes to reduce lock contention. Could be automatic policy.
- If memory pressure is the limiting factor, evaluate approximate LRU with bloom filter to avoid full prefix scans during eviction.

End of run — will pair with Kyla at 10:30 PT.

CR: tags for follow-up: #kv-evict #lock-contention #ttl-experiment
